title: The pip survives the dig now
question: The ringed pip is delivered at frame 91,806 and is still standing at 92,040 (234 frames later, against 5 before this fix) -- the dig verb no longer clears it as spoil. Does it read as "safe from the colony" even though it has not sprouted?
context_md:
Round 28, second half (`Reports/lanes/evolution-lab-garden-fix.md`). Diagnosis: the dig verb's own `ground` test could not tell a live seed from ordinary dirt (`pip` is `Powder`-kind), so it was clearing delivered pips as spoil with no counter seeing it -- confirmed by tracing this exact mechanism and by a guard test put back red before being trusted. Fixed at the dig dispatch site: a cell that is organism-owned `CellType::Seed` is skipped rather than dug.

Measured 3 seeds x 120,000 frames, played bed: the dig-diverted-seed counter fires 6/22/26 times per seed (the mechanism was real and is now closed). But `pip_checks` -- first Germinate evaluation -- is still 0 on every seed. This pip (seed 3) is the longest-surviving example across both rounds: it rolls a little as a Powder, stands for roughly 400 frames total, and then still rots (`pips_rotted`), because the whole carried span's decay hazard is settled in one roll at the moment of delivery, and a long carry (this one: over 1,000 frames) can lose that roll before the cell has stood for a single tick of Germinate's own schedule. So the dig fix is real and verified, and the loop's next blocker is decay racing the germinate check, not predation.
